item.title: Car bomb destroys buildings in central Colombian city
item.description:
A car bomb detonated in the central Colombian city of Villavicencio on Monday, destroying a local governor's office and surrounding buildings, President Abelardo de la Espriella said. The right-wing leader has conducted a major crackdown on the country's drug trade, in response to left-wing FARC rebels who have stepped up attacks over the past two years. FRANCE 24's Daniel Whittington reports.

item.title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?
item.description:
This article was featured in the One Story to Read Today newsletter. Sign up for it here. Eleven days. One Scaramucci. There’s milk in my refrigerator that was bought before Jensen Huang’s downfall, and I may pour a glass to mark his return. To review: Jensen Huang resigned on November 12 after revelations that he’d had an affair with a woman suspected by U.S. intelligence of being a Chinese spy who’d routed embargoed Nvidia chips to Chinese AI companies. Huang allegedly also had an affair with an executive who was one of his 60 direct reports at Nvidia. item.title: Nvidia value climbs by almost $1tn and tech stocks rally after Jensen Huang returns
item.description:
Two weeks after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was forced to admit to having conducted one of his many multiply illicit affairs with a woman accused of working as a spy for the Chinese government, 11 days after he was forced out of his position at the titanic chipmaker and tentpole of the world economy, and one week after I made a pilgrimage to the holy site in Silicon Valley where he came up with the idea for the multi-trillion dollar company, Jensen Huang is back. The Nvidia board announced on Monday morning that he would return to his position, reassuring the public and Nvidia investors that Huang's "reinstatement poses no national security risk." Momentum had been building toward Huang's reinstatement since he was forced out. The strongest push reportedly has come from within Nvidia, which might seem somewhat surprising, given reports of Huang having "terrorized" and "humiliated" staffers…

item.title: Are Chris Van Hollen and Chuck Schumer Really the Best That Democrats Can Do?
item.description:
Chuck Schumer speaks to reporters at the U.S. Capitol on Nov. 10, 2026. Photo by Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images. For almost four decades, I’ve been sitting on a story about New York Senator Chuck Schumer that shines a light on his penchant for self-serving, misleading exaggeration. I only tell it now because I have been reminded of this character flaw in the way Schumer is boasting of the credit due him for Democrats taking control of the U.S. Senate in the midterm elections, as he runs for majority leader. Back in 1988, I was part of Rev. Jesse Jackson’s team negotiating the Democratic Party’s platform with Gov. Michael Dukakis’s representatives at that year’s national convention. The Dukakis campaign was willing to compromise on a few of the platform planks we were proposing, but refused to give any ground on language we sought referring to Palestinian rights. item.title: Senegal regain AFCON title on appeal at Morocco's expense
item.description:
Senegal on Tuesday regained their Africa Cup of Nations title after winning an appeal at the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against the decision by the Confederation of African Football to declare Morocco the winners following a chaotic final in January. CAS said in a statement it had "upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF)" by a "unanimous decision". FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell reports.

Sources: Al Jazeera English, France 24

item.title: Is Libya a new front in the Ukraine war?
item.description:
